target.title: fix(discord): bound stalled probe response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord probe checks could hang after the `getMe` request returned response headers but the JSON response body stopped producing data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord probe now reads the successful `getMe` JSON body through the bounded response reader with the existing 16 MiB cap and a per-chunk timeout tied to the probe timeout. Existing non-OK handling, malformed JSON wording, and probe result flow are preserved.

## User Impact

Discord configuration checks now fail quickly on a stalled probe body instead of leaving users waiting on an unbounded read.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/probe.intents.test.ts` (10 tests passed)
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Claude autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
### Exact-head controlled-network proof

Exact head: `f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457`.

Command:

```text
PROOF_HEAD=f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457 HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost timeout 30s node --import tsx scratchpad/discord-probe-current-head-proof.mts
```

The temporary harness was removed after the run. It called production `probeDiscord()`, using the existing fetch seam only to route Discord API URLs to a loopback `node:http` server. The underlying client was real Node fetch; no mocked `Response`, Discord traffic, or credentials were used.

Redacted transcript:

```text
proof: exact-head=f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457 production Discord probe
probe: mode=normal ok=true error=null bot=bot-1 elapsed=42ms
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 120ms operation=fetchWithTimeout
probe: mode=header-stall ok=false error=request timed out elapsed=196ms
server: response closed mode=header-stall writableEnded=false
probe: mode=body-stall ok=false error=discord.probe.getMe: JSON response stalled after 120ms elapsed=129ms
server: response closed mode=body-stall writableEnded=false
probe: mode=slow-trickle ok=true error=null bot=bot-1 elapsed=1450ms
probe: mode=normal ok=true error=null bot=bot-1 elapsed=3ms
proof: current-head real HTTP assertions passed
```

Observed: a request stalled before headers aborts and closes its socket; a response that sends headers and a partial JSON body and then stops aborts through the production probe reader and closes its socket; a later normal probe succeeds. All assertions passed; exit 0.

Known limits: this is controlled local HTTP transport proof, not live Discord. Current head enforces an idle/per-chunk timeout, not a total response deadline: a body sending one chunk every 40 ms completed after 1450 ms with `timeoutMs=120`. This proof therefore establishes cleanup for a body that stops producing data and does not claim protection from an indefinitely slow trickle. The exact command referenced a temporary uncommitted harness that has been removed.
